entities.summary:
The Internet Archive is an American non-profit digital library founded in 1996 by Brewster Kahle to preserve web pages, books, audio, and video at planetary scale. Based in San Francisco, it is famous for the Wayback Machine’s snapshots of the changing web.

Operating at the intersection of librarianship, copyright law, and open-access activism, the Archive became infrastructure for historians, journalists, and the public—while facing litigation over digital lending. Its mission treats cultural memory as a commons under threat from link rot and enclosure.

The Internet Archive is among the defining memory institutions of the digital age.
